original_question: For dimensions n >= 3, prove the existence of a cone whose sail realizes a single prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure.
target_in_paper: §3.3, Problem 14 (the concluding problem on constructing generic cones): "Prove the existence of a cone for a single non-periodic combinatorial structure (n\ge 3)."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right open problem: it is about dimensions n >= 3, it is existential rather than classificatory, it concerns a cone together with its sail, and it asks for realization of one prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure rather than a periodic/fundamental-domain question or a face-classification question.
missing_details: The ambient setting is Euclidean space R^n with the standard integer lattice Z^n and origin 0.
A "cone" here means one of the cones determined by an arrangement of n hyperplanes through the origin in general position (§2.1).
The term "sail" must be understood in the sense of Definition 2.2, not as an informal polyhedral boundary; the paper treats several standard sail constructions under that definition.
The intended regime is the non-periodic generic case [G] of §3.1: the cone is non-algebraic and has no integer points on its faces.
In that case [G], the sail is expected to be non-periodic and combinatorially polyhedral; this is the hidden assumption behind speaking of its combinatorial structure.

The paper's nearby context says the question is open for the main standard sail models, including the Klein and Minkowski-Voronoi cases, and more generally for all standard choices covered by Definition 2.2; your draft does not say which notion of sail is being used.

To stay paper-faithful, the problem should not be strengthened to realization of every prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure; the paper only asks for existence for a single prescribed structure.

The contrast with the ordinary one-dimensional/standard continued-fraction case should be kept implicit or noted: the paper says the analogous problem is trivial there, so the real content is the multidimensional case n >= 3.
refined_question: In the setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions in R^n with lattice Z^n, fix one of the standard notions of sail from Definition 2.2. For n >= 3, exhibit at least one explicitly prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure and prove that there exists a cone C arising from an arrangement of n hyperplanes through the origin in general position, in the non-periodic generic case [G] (that is, C is non-algebraic and its faces contain no integer points), whose sail realizes exactly that prescribed non-periodic combinatorial structure.
justification: This paper is a short list of open problems rather than a paper built around Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3, and your draft clearly targets §3.3, Problem 14, whose wording it nearly paraphrases. The surrounding paragraph after Problem 14 explains the intended scope: the problem is about constructing generic non-periodic cones, i.e. case [G] from §3.1, and the technical meaning of "sail" comes from Definition 2.2, with the Klein and Minkowski-Voronoi constructions as the main examples in Definitions 2.4 and 2.5. The refined version therefore adds only those implicit hypotheses needed to make the question stand alone, while avoiding the stronger and broader claim that every prescribed non-periodic structure should be realizable.
